4	
5	## Layout
6	
7	- `packages/contracts` - Zod schemas and types. Depends on zod only.
8	- `packages/domain` - pure logic over the contracts. No I/O.
9	- `packages/engine` - executor, run manager, node handlers, written against ports. `@graphgoblin/engine/testing` has fakes for every port.
10	- `packages/infrastructure` - Node implementations of the engine ports, one folder per concern (`src/sqlite`, `src/fs`, `src/process`, `src/http`, `src/scheduler`), each with its own `index.ts` and an `@graphgoblin/infrastructure/<folder>` subpath. Folders may import each other.
11	- `packages/adapter-*` - reserved for optional external-service adapters with their own dependency (`adapter-codex`, `adapter-jev`). New packages only at real boundaries: a different runtime, reuse by several apps, or an optional or licence-sensitive dependency (ADR-0014). Otherwise add a folder.
12	- `apps/*` - composition roots: `api`, `mcp`, `web`, `plugin-codex`, `plugin-claude`.
13	- `tooling/` - shared config and the repository gate scripts.
14	
15	Layer rules are enforced by `pnpm check:layers` (declared workspace dependencies) and `pnpm check:deps` (dependency-cruiser). Reach other packages only through their `@graphgoblin/*` entry points.
16	
17	Node 22 LTS is the supported runtime; installation, development and gates need Node 22.22.2 or later, and other majors are unsupported. Select it for the whole shell before running commands. On this Windows host that is the project-scoped runtime, leaving the machine's own Node untouched: `$env:PATH = "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\codex-runs\GraphGoblin\runtime\node-v22.23.4-win-x64;$env:PATH"` in PowerShell, or `export PATH="$HOME/.claude/codex-runs/GraphGoblin/runtime/node-v22.23.4-win-x64:$PATH"` in Git Bash. Confirm `node --version` reports `v22.22.2` or later. `.nvmrc`, CI and the container use major 22 (CI and the container take the latest 22.x); root `engines.node` and `devEngines.runtime` declare `^22.22.2`, with `onFail: error` refusing every pnpm command on an older Node 22 or another major. pnpm runs package scripts with the first `node` on PATH. Run gates through pnpm: calling `node_modules/.bin/turbo` directly bypasses this check, and Turbo's cache key ignores the running Node version. See ADR-0040 and ADR-0058.
18	
19	## Rules
20	
21	- `tooling` participates in the shared Vitest V8 coverage gate and the Turbo lint pipeline; its independent built-app acceptance suites remain separate.
22	- Every package must keep unit-test coverage at or above 90% of lines and branches. `pnpm test:coverage` fails otherwise. Do not lower thresholds or add exclusions beyond generated code.
23	- `pnpm typecheck` runs `tsc -b tsconfig.build.json && tsc -p tsconfig.json` in every TypeScript package (the web app runs `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`), so test files and fixtures are type-checked too; fix their types rather than casting to `any`. `tooling` is JavaScript: it has lint and coverage, not a typecheck task.
24	- Tests, lint, and typechecking need no prior build in the TypeScript packages: each lists a `development` export condition pointing at its TypeScript source, which TypeScript, Vitest, and ESLint resolve. Node at runtime loads `dist/`, so run `pnpm build` before starting an app. A new TypeScript workspace package must follow the same export-map shape. `tooling` tests drive the built API and web app: Turbo builds them first, and a direct package test needs `pnpm build` first.
25	- API subprocess tests build the API first through Turbo's `test` and `test:coverage` task dependencies.
26	- Only permissive licences (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC). `pnpm check:licenses` enforces the allowlist in `tooling/license-allowlist.json`; add a line to `docs/research/licenses.md` for every new dependency.
27	- Relative imports use explicit `.js` extensions (NodeNext). Zod 4: use `.prefault({})` for object defaults whose fields have defaults.
28	- Keep docs in sync: a behaviour change updates the relevant numbered doc; a decision change adds an ADR.
29	- Clean design over backward compatibility, until the owner says otherwise (2026-10-04): the product is not released and has no production users. Do not build compatibility schemas, deprecated input paths, tolerant parsing of old data shapes, or dual code paths. Change the contract to its clean shape. A schema change within the current format is an ordinary Drizzle migration that keeps existing data; Drizzle migrations are for schema changes only. 31	- Commits carry no assistant attribution of any kind.
32	
33	## Commands
34	
35	On Windows PowerShell, call `pnpm.cmd` (the default execution policy blocks `pnpm.ps1`); Git Bash and cmd can use `pnpm` directly.
36	
37	```
38	pnpm install

40	pnpm test:coverage
41	pnpm lint
42	pnpm docs:generate  # regenerate docs/reference after a node schema or route change

# Working in this repository

GraphGoblin is a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo in TypeScript. Read `docs/README.md` first; `docs/12-implementation-plan.md` says what is being built now and `docs/decisions/` records settled decisions.

## Layout

- `packages/contracts` - Zod schemas and types. Depends on zod only.
- `packages/domain` - pure logic over the contracts. No I/O.
- `packages/engine` - executor, run manager, node handlers, written against ports. `@graphgoblin/engine/testing` has fakes for every port.
- `packages/infrastructure` - Node implementations of the engine ports, one folder per concern (`src/sqlite`, `src/fs`, `src/process`, `src/http`, `src/scheduler`), each with its own `index.ts` and an `@graphgoblin/infrastructure/<folder>` subpath. Folders may import each other.
- `packages/adapter-*` - reserved for optional external-service adapters with their own dependency (`adapter-codex`, `adapter-jev`). New packages only at real boundaries: a different runtime, reuse by several apps, or an optional or licence-sensitive dependency (ADR-0014). Otherwise add a folder.
- `apps/*` - composition roots: `api`, `mcp`, `web`, `plugin-codex`, `plugin-claude`.
- `tooling/` - shared config and the repository gate scripts.

Layer rules are enforced by `pnpm check:layers` (declared workspace dependencies) and `pnpm check:deps` (dependency-cruiser). Reach other packages only through their `@graphgoblin/*` entry points.

Node 22 LTS is the supported runtime; installation, development and gates need Node 22.22.2 or later, and other majors are unsupported. Select it for the whole shell before running commands. On this Windows host that is the project-scoped runtime, leaving the machine's own Node untouched: `$env:PATH = "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\codex-runs\GraphGoblin\runtime\node-v22.23.4-win-x64;$env:PATH"` in PowerShell, or `export PATH="$HOME/.claude/codex-runs/GraphGoblin/runtime/node-v22.23.4-win-x64:$PATH"` in Git Bash. Confirm `node --version` reports `v22.22.2` or later. `.nvmrc`, CI and the container use major 22 (CI and the container take the latest 22.x); root `engines.node` and `devEngines.runtime` declare `^22.22.2`, with `onFail: error` refusing every pnpm command on an older Node 22 or another major. pnpm runs package scripts with the first `node` on PATH. Run gates through pnpm: calling `node_modules/.bin/turbo` directly bypasses this check, and Turbo's cache key ignores the running Node version. See ADR-0040 and ADR-0058.

## Rules

- `tooling` participates in the shared Vitest V8 coverage gate and the Turbo lint pipeline; its independent built-app acceptance suites remain separate.
- Every package must keep unit-test coverage at or above 90% of lines and branches. `pnpm test:coverage` fails otherwise. Do not lower thresholds or add exclusions beyond generated code.
- `pnpm typecheck` runs `tsc -b tsconfig.build.json && tsc -p tsconfig.json` in every TypeScript package (the web app runs `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`), so test files and fixtures are type-checked too; fix their types rather than casting to `any`. `tooling` is JavaScript: it has lint and coverage, not a typecheck task.
- Tests, lint, and typechecking need no prior build in the TypeScript packages: each lists a `development` export condition pointing at its TypeScript source, which TypeScript, Vitest, and ESLint resolve. Node at runtime loads `dist/`, so run `pnpm build` before starting an app. A new TypeScript workspace package must follow the same export-map shape. `tooling` tests drive the built API and web app: Turbo builds them first, and a direct package test needs `pnpm build` first.
- API subprocess tests build the API first through Turbo's `test` and `test:coverage` task dependencies.
- Only permissive licences (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC). `pnpm check:licenses` enforces the allowlist in `tooling/license-allowlist.json`; add a line to `docs/research/licenses.md` for every new dependency.
- Relative imports use explicit `.js` extensions (NodeNext). Zod 4: use `.prefault({})` for object defaults whose fields have defaults.
- Keep docs in sync: a behaviour change updates the relevant numbered doc; a decision change adds an ADR.
- Clean design over backward compatibility, until the owner says otherwise (2026-10-04): the product is not released and has no production users. Do not build compatibility schemas, deprecated input paths, tolerant parsing of old data shapes, or dual code paths. Change the contract to its clean shape. A schema change within the current format is an ordinary Drizzle migration that keeps existing data; Drizzle migrations are for schema changes only. Stored content that a change makes invalid is never rewritten by migration code: the CHANGELOG upgrade note says which stored values to correct and how (for example the SQL), and the orchestrator corrects the owner's store by hand (ADR-0062). A change of the stored, export or device-draft format moves the current format and refuses older data clearly, with no converter, and the owner resets with `--reset` (ADR-0042); say so, and what exports or clients must change, in the CHANGELOG upgrade notes.
- Before picking up a GitHub issue, read `docs/15-issue-workflow.md` for its gate, routing, and delivery rules.
- Commits carry no assistant attribution of any kind.

## Commands

On Windows PowerShell, call `pnpm.cmd` (the default execution policy blocks `pnpm.ps1`); Git Bash and cmd can use `pnpm` directly.

```
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm test:coverage
pnpm lint
pnpm docs:generate  # regenerate docs/reference after a node schema or route change
pnpm check          # typecheck, lint, layers, deps, coverage, licences, generated docs
```

1	# D193 — Correct #364 probe precedence and preserve help-only causes
2	
3	Accept both source-established findings from final independent Astra scan2 at a04f6661a74a727e6c963d8648ea2998bb6dbe7b. Its CHANGES_REQUIRED report SHA-2564948e0b8d2c46044fa16da1fc04e77547c87ac2c40e31c75b2b34e386a95c637 remains intact. F1 is P2: output loss can leave a nonzero/null auth probe with partial auth-like text, and diagnostic inference currently runs before the output-failure guard. F2 is P3: a successful version probe followed by a help-only start refusal or output loss loses the newly established fixed cause in an older generic help wrapper. These combined cases were not executed by the auditor; do not describe them as native reproductions.
4	
5	Select actual Claude Opus5.5/xhigh implementation in the existing adapter. For probes, check established output failure before stdout/stderr readiness inference, preserving stronger termination, cancellation, start-refusal, deadline, overflow and callback outcomes. Do not infer a signed-out fact from incomplete output. Keep completed genuine auth refusals and all turn submission/recovery behavior unchanged.
6

GraphGoblin is a progressive web application plus a gateway backend for designing, running, and observing agent **loops**. A loop is a graph of nodes. Triggers start it. Decision nodes route it. Inferencing nodes hand work to an agent harness. Script and context-mutation nodes shape the shared **context thread**. Wait and heartbeat nodes park it. Subloops nest it. An exit node decides when it is done, what it returns, and where the result goes.

GraphGoblin is built for AI engineers. AI-driven development lifecycle (AIDLC) pipelines are the first use case, not the only one. Nothing in the core should assume GitHub, pull requests, or software engineering.

1	# 15 - Issue workflow
2	
3	GitHub issues are the shared work queue for this repository's development pipeline. Every non-epic issue carries at least one gate label. A triager sets the type, area, gate, QA, and routing labels from the issue and its dependencies.
4	
5	## Gates
6	
7	- `aidlc-ready`: the issue may enter this repository's agent-led development pipeline. Its approved behaviour is accepted through independent agent review, tests appropriate to the acceptance criteria and independent QA: tests through public methods that directly establish a criterion are sufficient for that criterion, and API, native-process or browser evidence is added where a criterion needs it. Use for bug fixes, maintainability, chores, backend work and ordinary testable feature and UI work.
8	- `human-in-the-loop`: the work is implemented, reviewed, tested and merged through the same agent gates, and in addition a human exercises the merged build afterwards and records what they observed. Reserve it for feature work with substantial ambiguity, or behaviour whose correctness agents cannot readily verify with confidence. A UI change does not qualify merely because it changes a screen; a missing or failing test, or a known defect, is engineering work, not a reason for the label. Before applying it, record on the issue the feature, the specific ambiguity or verification limit, what public-interface tests and other agent evidence establish, and a concrete post-merge human QA checklist with expected observations. The label does not require a human review before merge and waives no technical gate.
9	- `needs-plan-approval`: for architecture changes and cutovers. An agent posts a written plan as an issue comment. A human approves by replacing this label with `plan-approved` and adding `aidlc-ready`, keeping `human-in-the-loop` when it applies.
10	- `plan-approved`: set by a human only, after reviewing the written plan.
11	
12	`aidlc-ready` describes delivery eligibility and `human-in-the-loop` describes a later human QA obligation, so the two may coexist; `needs-plan-approval` may be combined with either. Until 2026-10-21 this file described `human-in-the-loop` as a human review of the running product before merge, classified UI work under it as a whole and said it never combined with `aidlc-ready`. That wording was this repository's own metadata, not an owner requirement for objectively verifiable behaviour; the owner's clarification of 2026-10-21 (recorded in [#279](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/279)) supersedes it.
13	
14	## Post-merge human QA
15	
16	Every pull request for a `human-in-the-loop` issue carries a post-merge human QA checklist with expected observations and names an open tracking item (the issue itself or a linked QA item). The PR references that item as "Part of", never with a closing keyword, so the pipeline never closes it. After the merge a human exercises the merged build, records the commit or build, their observations and the outcome on the tracking item, and closes it. Human QA is tracked separately from implementation, review, agent QA, CI and merge, as one of: not required, pending merge, pending human QA, or completed with an evidence link. Agent evidence never completes the human step, and the human step never permits merging a known defect or bypassing a gate. A product decision that is needed to define correct behaviour goes to the owner as a concrete question with evidence, separately from post-merge QA.
17	
18	A delivery batch may carry an additional pre-merge sign-off gate (for example, a designated independent review session that must approve each PR at an exact head). Such a gate is recorded in the batch's register under `docs/delivery/` and is separate from post-merge human QA.
19	
20	## Parking markers
21	
22	Two labels take an issue out of the queue; neither is a gate, and an issue carrying one has no gate label until a human unparks it.
23	
24	- `backlog`: parked until further notice. Agents do not plan or implement it.
25	- `needs-refinement`: the problem itself still needs human-driven refinement in a working session with the owner before any plan or implementation.
26	
27	## QA scope
28	
29	- `qa:touched-systems`: enumerate every system the change touches, test each with positive and negative cases, and record pass/fail results with evidence in both the PR and issue.

# 15 - Issue workflow

GitHub issues are the shared work queue for this repository's development pipeline. Every non-epic issue carries at least one gate label. A triager sets the type, area, gate, QA, and routing labels from the issue and its dependencies.

## Gates

- `aidlc-ready`: the issue may enter this repository's agent-led development pipeline. Its approved behaviour is accepted through independent agent review, tests appropriate to the acceptance criteria and independent QA: tests through public methods that directly establish a criterion are sufficient for that criterion, and API, native-process or browser evidence is added where a criterion needs it. Use for bug fixes, maintainability, chores, backend work and ordinary testable feature and UI work.
- `human-in-the-loop`: the work is implemented, reviewed, tested and merged through the same agent gates, and in addition a human exercises the merged build afterwards and records what they observed. Reserve it for feature work with substantial ambiguity, or behaviour whose correctness agents cannot readily verify with confidence. A UI change does not qualify merely because it changes a screen; a missing or failing test, or a known defect, is engineering work, not a reason for the label. Before applying it, record on the issue the feature, the specific ambiguity or verification limit, what public-interface tests and other agent evidence establish, and a concrete post-merge human QA checklist with expected observations. The label does not require a human review before merge and waives no technical gate.
- `needs-plan-approval`: for architecture changes and cutovers. An agent posts a written plan as an issue comment. A human approves by replacing this label with `plan-approved` and adding `aidlc-ready`, keeping `human-in-the-loop` when it applies.
- `plan-approved`: set by a human only, after reviewing the written plan.

`aidlc-ready` describes delivery eligibility and `human-in-the-loop` describes a later human QA obligation, so the two may coexist; `needs-plan-approval` may be combined with either. Until 2026-10-21 this file described `human-in-the-loop` as a human review of the running product before merge, classified UI work under it as a whole and said it never combined with `aidlc-ready`. That wording was this repository's own metadata, not an owner requirement for objectively verifiable behaviour; the owner's clarification of 2026-10-21 (recorded in [#279](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/279)) supersedes it.

## Post-merge human QA

Every pull request for a `human-in-the-loop` issue carries a post-merge human QA checklist with expected observations and names an open tracking item (the issue itself or a linked QA item). The PR references that item as "Part of", never with a closing keyword, so the pipeline never closes it. After the merge a human exercises the merged build, records the commit or build, their observations and the outcome on the tracking item, and closes it. Human QA is tracked separately from implementation, review, agent QA, CI and merge, as one of: not required, pending merge, pending human QA, or completed with an evidence link. Agent evidence never completes the human step, and the human step never permits merging a known defect or bypassing a gate. A product decision that is needed to define correct behaviour goes to the owner as a concrete question with evidence, separately from post-merge QA.

A delivery batch may carry an additional pre-merge sign-off gate (for example, a designated independent review session that must approve each PR at an exact head). Such a gate is recorded in the batch's register under `docs/delivery/` and is separate from post-merge human QA.

## Parking markers

Two labels take an issue out of the queue; neither is a gate, and an issue carrying one has no gate label until a human unparks it.

- `backlog`: parked until further notice. Agents do not plan or implement it.
- `needs-refinement`: the problem itself still needs human-driven refinement in a working session with the owner before any plan or implementation.

## QA scope

- `qa:touched-systems`: enumerate every system the change touches, test each with positive and negative cases, and record pass/fail results with evidence in both the PR and issue.
- `qa:full-regression`: also retest the whole application end to end, covering positive and negative scenarios, and catalogue the results.

Name the QA agent in the issue body's Delivery section, not with a label.

Retain QA evidence under `docs/qa/` with repository-relative citations and preserve raw JSON, YAML and JavaScript/TypeScript bytes so recorded hashes remain valid; `.prettierignore` excludes those artifacts while QA Markdown remains formatted.

## Model routing

The triager sets one `impl:<model>` label and one `review:<model>` label. Use the following tiers, with xhigh reasoning:

| Tier | Model             | Use                         |
| ---- | ----------------- | --------------------------- |
| 1    | `gpt-6-luna`      | Mundane work                |
| 2    | `gpt-6.1-sol`     | Default work                |
| 3    | `claude-opus-5.5` | Harder work and sign-off    |
| 4    | `gpt-6-astra`     | Hardest work and escalation |

Whatever model family implements the change, the other family reviews it: OpenAI models are reviewed by Claude, and Claude is reviewed by an OpenAI model. If a worker cannot finish, escalate to the next tier.

## Types, areas, and milestones

Every issue has one type: `type:bug`, `type:feature`, `type:ui-polish`, `type:architecture`, `type:chore`, `type:research`, or `type:epic`. Area labels locate the affected part of the product: `area:web`, `area:editor`, `area:settings`, `area:api`, `area:engine`, `area:contracts`, `area:design-system`, `area:templates`, `area:integrations`, `area:installer`, or `area:harness`.

Milestones are `Pre-merge #151` for work that must land before the feature PR merges, `After merge: evaluate and stabilise` for product evaluation, the architecture sweep and the cutovers they require (this milestone blocks further feature work), and `Later` for queued and long-term work, with most items parked under `backlog`.

Epics carry `type:epic` and area labels only; pipelines ignore them. Each child issue starts its body with `Part of #<epic-number>`, and the epic lists its child issues.

## Development pipeline

An issue is picked up according to its gate label. The implementer named by its `impl:` label works in an isolated branch. The reviewer named by its `review:` label reviews the diff and comes from the opposite model family. A QA agent tests according to the `qa:` label and records results in the PR and the issue. `human-in-the-loop` issues additionally get human QA of the merged build, tracked as described above. `needs-plan-approval` issues get a human-approved plan before implementation. When a human QA step is required before an issue closes (by the label, or by the owner in a comment on the issue), its pull requests reference it as "Part of" rather than "Closes", the pipeline never closes it, and the human who exercised the merged build closes it with a comment saying what was checked.

The label names and this process are specific to this repository and are not used by the product's template loops, which users run against their own repositories with their own configurable trigger label and role models (tracked in [the AIDLC template loops epic on GitHub](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20label%3Atype%3Aepic%20label%3Aarea%3Atemplates)).

policies keep their existing meanings. Session lookup filters by harness before selecting the
newest matching session, so a Codex session is never passed to Claude or vice versa. The same
resolved request is used for normal and structured-output repair turns. Version, help, and authentication probes run in a fresh empty temporary directory; only the actual turn uses the authored working directory.

**Start refusals (#364).** A spawn `ENOENT` does not say which operand failed: on Windows 11 with
Node 22.23.4, a missing working directory, one that is a file and an existing one longer than 258
characters are all refused with the same `ENOENT` as a missing executable, and Node attributes
each to the executable. After an actual refusal (Node created no process), the runner makes one
read-only observation of the request's own executable and working directory and returns only a
closed cause. The executable counts as missing only when its configured path is fully qualified
and that path and its `.com` and `.exe` forms, the names Windows process start tries, are all
absent or folders; an executable named without a full path is never resolved through `PATH`. A
working directory that is absent (or below a file) or is not a folder is established from its own
metadata. An existing folder establishes nothing, because it can still be unstartable, and a read
that fails for any other reason leaves the cause unknown. The adapter reports only what was
established, in fixed text without paths:

| Established                              | Preflight                                                                                                                                                 | Turn                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Executable missing                       | `cli-missing`: "Claude CLI was not found at the configured path."                                                                                         | `HARNESS_NOT_INSTALLED` (restorable), raised by the turn's own readiness check                                                                            |
| Turn working directory missing or a file | Not applicable                                                                                                                                            | `HARNESS_INVALID_CONFIGURATION`: "Claude could not be started because the working directory does not exist" (or "is not a folder"); pinned, not resumable |
| Check folder missing or a file           | `unknown`: "Claude CLI could not be started because its temporary check folder does not exist." (or "is not a folder")                                    | The same detail as `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED`; the check folder is never configuration                                                                         |
| Nothing, path over 258 characters        | `unknown`: "... from its temporary check folder, whose path (from TEMP or TMP) is longer than the 258 characters Windows allows for a working directory." | `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED`: "Claude could not be started (ENOENT); the working directory path is longer than the 258 characters Windows allows"                |
| Nothing                                  | `unknown`: "Claude CLI could not be started (ENOENT)." (or the `EACCES`/`UNKNOWN` code)                                                                   | `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED`: "Claude could not be started (ENOENT); check the Claude executable's path and permissions and the working directory"               |

Every refusal stays `definitely-not-submitted`, and the turn uses the working directory exactly as
given. Unconfirmed termination and cancellation keep their precedence; an abort or deadline that
arrives during the observation reports the refusal at once, without a cause and without a timeout.
A later error event of a started process, such as a failed kill, is not a refusal. From 260
characters Windows also fails the refused process's stdout and stderr pipes (`read ENOTCONN`); the
runner ignores pipe faults of a process that never started, where they previously escaped as an
uncaught exception. A started process's stdout or stderr failure stops its tree and fails the turn
(`HARNESS_TURN_FAILED`, delivery uncertain, ahead of any recognised stderr refusal, because lost
output can hide acceptance) or the check ("Claude CLI check output could not be read."). The 258-character wording states the path's length against the documented limit; it is
not proof of the cause.

The CLI streams JSON lines. GraphGoblin records bounded progress, usage, the transcript artifact,
and a policy-evidence item when transcript capture is enabled. Provider response bodies and raw
stderr are not included in diagnostics. Cancellation owns the CLI process tree; if termination
cannot be confirmed, the run fails with `HARNESS_TERMINATION_UNCONFIRMED` and is not reported as
cancelled. Engine and persistence failures retain their original cause and stop the active initial or repair session; unconfirmed cleanup takes precedence. Claude is not a decision evaluator: decision evaluation, exit configuration, and
the separate Codex structured port remain unchanged. Inference schema validation uses the authored repair and failure policy for either harness, preserving the native candidate (including null or a missing candidate) rather than substituting final text. API-provider support remains future work tracked by
[#100](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/100).

`system/commands_changed` and `system/ui_invalidate` can precede or follow init. UI invalidation
requires a nonempty string `event` of at most 100 characters and valid UUID-shaped `uuid` and
`session_id`. Both metadata records must use the same session as each other and init. They emit
no progress, session, prompt-delivery or execution evidence. Verified init alone announces the
session. Status, partial-message and rate-limit metadata also carry no execution evidence.
Before init, only init and the two validated metadata records are accepted. After init,

# Changelog

All notable changes to GraphGoblin. The design is in [docs/](docs/README.md); the user guide is [docs/guide/](docs/guide/README.md).

## Unreleased

- Claude no longer reports a missing CLI when Windows refused the working directory (#364).
  Windows refuses a missing working directory, one that is a file and one longer than 258
  characters with the same spawn `ENOENT` as a missing executable. After a refused start the
  adapter now reads, without changing anything, the configured executable's full path (with the
  `.com` and `.exe` forms Windows also tries) and the working directory, and reports only what
  that establishes: `cli-missing`/`HARNESS_NOT_INSTALLED` when that executable path is absent;
  `HARNESS_INVALID_CONFIGURATION` (not resumable) when a turn's working directory does not exist
  or is not a folder; otherwise an `unknown` preflight or `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED` turn whose fixed
  text names the 258-character limit when the path exceeds it, or both possible causes. An
  executable named without a full path that cannot be started is now `unknown` rather than
  `cli-missing`. Refused starts stay `definitely-not-submitted`; cancellation, deadlines and
  unconfirmed termination keep precedence; no message contains a path or native error text. A
  refused start in a working directory of 260 characters or more no longer raises an uncaught
  `read ENOTCONN` pipe error that could stop the API, and a later error of a started CLI, such
  as a failed kill, is no longer taken for a refused start. No store, export or contract change.

- Clarify that an enabled Codex model and a ready preflight do not establish current access
  for the API user's login and provider endpoint. Recognized Codex inference-turn refusals retain
  the provider's explanation; LLM decisions retain only a safe failure category. The guide
  describes deliberate supported-model/login selection without automatic fallback or an
  API-key-only promise (#427).
- Reconcile Codex sandbox documentation and source comments: the authored sandbox permission
  level is explicit, while Windows backend selection remains inherited unless explicitly
  overridden. No sandbox permissions or backend behavior changed (#365).

# #364 author report — truthful Claude process-start diagnostics

Worker: Claude Code Opus 5.5 (xhigh), intent 4 unit U4.5. Checkout
`G:/ggq/gg-i4-364-claude-start/GraphGoblin`, branch `codex/gg-i4-364-claude-start`, base
`02351e2fb932b3be44e7cc3fb3943a61d568226c`. Uncommitted, unstaged, unpushed; no issue touched.
Evidence: `evidence/` (logs, probe JSON, mutation logs, `candidate.diff`), scripts: `scripts/`.

## Status

Bounded candidate complete. All focused checks pass. Package-wide infrastructure coverage could not
be evaluated on this host: 50 pre-existing symlink tests fail with `EPERM` (environment, below).
No engine/contract/other-package change was needed.

## Proven defect (native, before the change)

Windows 11 + Node 22.23.4, harmless `node.exe`, disposable paths (`evidence/native-spawn-probe.json`):

| Case                                              | Spawn result                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| valid binary, valid cwd; 240/258-char cwd         | starts (child cwd length 240/258)              |
| missing cwd, cwd below missing parent             | `ENOENT`, `error.path` = binary                |
| cwd is a file, cwd below a file                   | `ENOENT`, `error.path` = binary                |
| existing cwd of 259 chars                         | `ENOENT`                                       |
| existing cwd of 260 / 300 chars                   | `ENOENT` + stdout/stderr `read ENOTCONN`       |
| missing absolute binary, missing bare name        | `ENOENT`                                       |
| binary path is a folder                           | `ENOENT`                                       |

So `ENOENT` (and `error.path`) cannot identify the failing operand. Probe attempt 1 had no stream
error handlers and the plain Node process died on the unhandled `read ENOTCONN`
(`evidence/native-spawn-probe-attempt1-crash.stderr.txt`, exit 1).

Unmodified source through the real runner/harness (`evidence/baseline-unmodified-verbose.log`):
- long-TEMP preflight (check folder 259/300) → `cli-missing`, "Claude CLI was not found at the
  configured path. Install the Claude CLI or set GG_CLAUDE_BINARY…" although the binary exists;
- turn in a 300-char workspace → `HARNESS_NOT_INSTALLED` "The installed Claude executable could
  not be started…";
- 8 uncaught `read ENOTCONN` exceptions from `runClaudeProcess` (cwd ≥ 260). `apps/api` has no
  `uncaughtException` handler (grep), so this would end the API process — inferred, the built API
  was not run.

## Change (only `packages/infrastructure/src/claude/` + docs)

`process.ts` (runner, privacy boundary kept — closed codes only):
- `spawnCode` only for an **actual** refusal (`child.pid === undefined`). A later child `error` of
  a started process (e.g. failed kill) no longer becomes `spawnCode: UNKNOWN` →
  `definitely-not-submitted` (controlled evidence only).
- After a refusal, one read-only `stat` observation → closed `startRefusal`:
  `executable-missing` only for `ENOENT` + fully qualified binary (`isAbsolute` and
  `resolve === normalize`) whose path, `.com` and `.exe` forms (libuv's Windows candidates; POSIX:
  path only) are all ENOENT/ENOTDIR or folders; `working-directory-missing` (ENOENT/ENOTDIR) or
  `working-directory-not-directory`. Any other read error → `unknown` (no cause). Existing folder
  → no cause. No PATH resolution, no subprocess probe, no fallback.
- Abort/deadline during the observation: settle immediately with the refusal, no cause, no
  `timedOut`, no kill timer. `close` after a refusal is ignored (refusal path settles once).
- stdout/stderr/stdin `error` of a never-started child ignored (fixes the ENOTCONN crash); a
  started child's stdout/stderr failure → `outputFailed`, tree killed.

`harness.ts` (fixed text, no paths):

| Established                    | Preflight                                                        | Turn                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| executable missing             | `cli-missing` (text unchanged)                                   | `HARNESS_NOT_INSTALLED` (restorable)                                                          |
| turn cwd missing / not folder  | —                                                                | `HARNESS_INVALID_CONFIGURATION` "…working directory does not exist / is not a folder…" (pinned) |
| check folder missing / file    | `unknown` "…temporary check folder does not exist / is not a folder." | `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED` (never configuration)                                              |
| nothing, resolved cwd > 258    | `unknown` "…check folder, whose path (from TEMP or TMP) is longer than the 258 characters Windows allows…" | `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED` "…working directory path is longer than the 258 characters Windows allows" |
| nothing                        | `unknown` "Claude CLI could not be started (ENOENT)."             | `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED` "Claude could not be started (ENOENT); check the Claude executable's path and permissions and the working directory" |

All refusals keep `definitely-not-submitted`; precedence unchanged (termination-unconfirmed >
abort > refusal > timeout/overflow …). `outputFailed` added to the turn's transport-cutoff
precedence block (ahead of stderr refusals, since lost stdout can hide acceptance) and to probe
outcomes ("Claude CLI check output could not be read.").

Docs: `docs/06-harness-integration.md` (start-refusal paragraph + table, Windows paragraph link),
`docs/guide/07-troubleshooting.md` (row rewritten to new wording, new turn row, `unknown` row;
column widths kept), `CHANGELOG.md` (Unreleased entry, no upgrade action). Fixture `turn-cli.mjs`
gains a `success` scenario returning the child's actual cwd.

## Tests added/changed

- `start-refusal.test.ts` (new, native, real runner + `node.exe` fake CLI, canary
  `PRIVATE_CANARY_364` in paths/TEMP/prompt): ordinary success in requested cwd; missing cwd →
  INVALID_CONFIGURATION, cwd passed as-is; cwd is a file (win32); existing 258 (starts, finalText ==
  cwd) / 259 / 260 / 300 (TURN_FAILED long text, no unhandled error) (win32); long-TEMP preflight
  258 ready / 259 / 300 unknown + check folder removed (win32); absolute missing binary → preflight
  `cli-missing` exact text, turn NOT_INSTALLED, no turn spawned; binary path is a folder →
  `cli-missing` (win32); bare missing name → `unknown`; engine-backed run failures: missing cwd →
  `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED`, `adapterCode: HARNESS_INVALID_CONFIGURATION`, `resumable: false`,
  `definitely-not-submitted`; missing binary → `HARNESS_NOT_INSTALLED`, `resumable: true`.
  Privacy: no canary, root path, `spawn `, `errno`, `syscall` in events/errors/preflight/failure.
- `process-failure.test.ts` (controlled, mocked spawn + `stat`): candidate rule, file/EACCES/
  unclassified binary reads leave cause open, cwd missing/ENOTDIR/file/folder/EACCES/EPERM, bare &
  relative names never stat'ed, EACCES never claims absence, abort/deadline during observation,
  pipe faults + close after refusal, failed-kill error after start, stdout/stderr failure of a
  started child. Mocked child now carries a pid (it models a started process).
- `harness.test.ts`: every turn/probe mapping with exact text, cwd passed unchanged, cancellation
  ahead of diagnosis, output failure ahead of refusal, long check folder wording, unreadable check
  output; the existing "missing executable" case now carries `executable-missing` and a new
  "unexplained start refusal" case asserts `unknown`/`HARNESS_TURN_FAILED`.
- `process.test.ts`: existing native missing-executable test asserts `executable-missing`.

Negative controls (`evidence/mutations/`, each restored byte-identically, SHA-256 checked):
M1 drop stdio error handlers → 8 unhandled errors, exit 1; M2 ENOENT ⇒ executable-missing → 18
failures; M3 no started-guard → 1; M4 literal name only → 4; M5 abort waits for observation → 2;
M6 uncertain read ⇒ missing → 4; M7 check folder as configuration → 2; M8 output failure below
refusal → 2.

## Checks (project Node v22.23.4 verified first; `pnpm.cmd` in PowerShell)

| Command                                                                  | Result |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------ |
| `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`                                         | 0 (no lockfile change) |
| existing `src/claude` tests after production change, before test updates | 2 expected failures (ENOENT⇒cli-missing case; mocked child w/o pid) — `existing-tests-after-prod-change.log` |
| `process-failure.test.ts` first run                                      | 1 failure: my table captured `Stats` before `beforeAll`; fixed with runtime tokens |
| `pnpm run typecheck` (infrastructure)                                    | 0 |
| `pnpm run lint` (infrastructure)                                         | 0 |
| `prettier --check` changed files/docs                                    | 0 (after `--write` on my files; bases were clean) |
| `vitest run src/claude --coverage` (include `src/claude/**`, disposable home) | 259 passed, 2 skipped; 99.24 st / 98.15 br / 100 fn / 99.82 ln; exit 0 |
| `pnpm run test:coverage` (whole infrastructure, disposable home)         | exit 1: 50 `fs.symlink` EPERM (chat-audio 4, voice 46) + 1 `EBUSY` WAL unlink (sqlite/chat); all claude tests passed; coverage not reported on failure |
| same 3 failing files without home redirect                               | 50 EPERM again (host has no `SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege`, Developer Mode unset); sqlite/chat passed (EBUSY not reproduced) |
| `pnpm run check:layers` / `check:deps`                                   | OK / 0 errors (4 pre-existing orphan warnings) |

Not run (per brief): full monorepo build/coverage, browser suite, `apps/api` tests (need an API
build; no API test uses `spawnCode` or the changed texts — grep). No paid/provider/network call.
The two existing tests that run the owner's installed `claude.exe` were skipped by pointing
`USERPROFILE`/`HOME` at an empty disposable folder (removed after; stayed empty), to avoid reading
the owner's real Claude auth/config.

## Remaining limits

- The 258-character wording is a length fact against the documented limit, not proof of cause;
  stat success never proves startability. Windows-specific native cases skip on other platforms;
  this run did not execute Linux CI.
- An executable named without a full path (PATH lookup) that fails to start is now `unknown`, not
  `cli-missing` (no resolver by contract).
- Observation races: a path changed between refusal and `stat` is reported as observed; uncertain
  reads report no cause.
- Synchronous spawn throws (Node throws for codes other than EACCES/EAGAIN/EMFILE/ENFILE/ENOENT,
  e.g. POSIX `ENOTDIR`) still reject the runner → generic `Claude turn failed`, delivery
  uncertain (conservative; unchanged; no Windows case observed).

## Decisions for root's catalogue (proposed, not blockers)

1. Unexplained refusal → `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED`, `retriable: false` (non-resumable for Claude, like
   existing EACCES/UNKNOWN). Previously ENOENT was `HARNESS_NOT_INSTALLED` (resumable) on a false
   claim. Alternative declined: `retriable: true` to keep resumability — would stretch
   "retriable" to a non-transient start failure.
2. Turn cwd missing/not a folder → `HARNESS_INVALID_CONFIGURATION` (pinned, non-resumable;
   engine shows `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED` + `adapterCode`). Alternative: generic `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED`
   (same resumability, less specific). Contract `WORKING_DIRECTORY_MISSING` exists but is unused;
   using it needs an engine mapping change (out of scope).
3. Included two fixes on the same start path beyond wording: unhandled ENOTCONN (natively proven)
   and the started-child error guard (controlled evidence only).

## Out-of-scope observations for root (not changed)

- Codex maps any `enoent` to `HARNESS_NOT_INSTALLED` (`packages/adapter-codex/src/events.ts:354`,
  `isolation.ts:177`) — same misdiagnosis class.
- `packages/infrastructure/src/process/scripts.ts` and `packages/adapter-codex/src/cli.ts` attach
  no stdout/stderr `error` handlers; the same uncaught ENOTCONN for a ≥260-char cwd is plausible
  but was not exercised.
- Host: symlink tests need Developer Mode or the symlink privilege; one transient SQLite `EBUSY`.

- `process.test.ts`: existing native missing-executable test asserts `executable-missing`.

Negative controls (`evidence/mutations/`, each restored byte-identically, SHA-256 checked):
M1 drop stdio error handlers → 8 unhandled errors, exit 1; M2 ENOENT ⇒ executable-missing → 18
failures; M3 no started-guard → 1; M4 literal name only → 4; M5 abort waits for observation → 2;
M6 uncertain read ⇒ missing → 4; M7 check folder as configuration → 2; M8 output failure below
refusal → 2.

## Checks (project Node v22.23.4 verified first; `pnpm.cmd` in PowerShell)

| Command                                                                  | Result |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------ |
| `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`                                         | 0 (no lockfile change) |
| existing `src/claude` tests after production change, before test updates | 2 expected failures (ENOENT⇒cli-missing case; mocked child w/o pid) — `existing-tests-after-prod-change.log` |
| `process-failure.test.ts` first run                                      | 1 failure: my table captured `Stats` before `beforeAll`; fixed with runtime tokens |
| `pnpm run typecheck` (infrastructure)                                    | 0 |
| `pnpm run lint` (infrastructure)                                         | 0 |
| `prettier --check` changed files/docs                                    | 0 (after `--write` on my files; bases were clean) |
| `vitest run src/claude --coverage` (include `src/claude/**`, disposable home) | 259 passed, 2 skipped; 99.24 st / 98.15 br / 100 fn / 99.82 ln; exit 0 |
| `pnpm run test:coverage` (whole infrastructure, disposable home)         | exit 1: 50 `fs.symlink` EPERM (chat-audio 4, voice 46) + 1 `EBUSY` WAL unlink (sqlite/chat); all claude tests passed; coverage not reported on failure |
| same 3 failing files without home redirect                               | 50 EPERM again (host has no `SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege`, Developer Mode unset); sqlite/chat passed (EBUSY not reproduced) |
| `pnpm run check:layers` / `check:deps`                                   | OK / 0 errors (4 pre-existing orphan warnings) |

Not run (per brief): full monorepo build/coverage, browser suite, `apps/api` tests (need an API
build; no API test uses `spawnCode` or the changed texts — grep). No paid/provider/network call.
The two existing tests that run the owner's installed `claude.exe` were skipped by pointing
`USERPROFILE`/`HOME` at an empty disposable folder (removed after; stayed empty), to avoid reading
the owner's real Claude auth/config.

## Remaining limits

- The 258-character wording is a length fact against the documented limit, not proof of cause;
  stat success never proves startability. Windows-specific native cases skip on other platforms;
  this run did not execute Linux CI.
- An executable named without a full path (PATH lookup) that fails to start is now `unknown`, not
  `cli-missing` (no resolver by contract).
- Observation races: a path changed between refusal and `stat` is reported as observed; uncertain
  reads report no cause.
- Synchronous spawn throws (Node throws for codes other than EACCES/EAGAIN/EMFILE/ENFILE/ENOENT,
  e.g. POSIX `ENOTDIR`) still reject the runner → generic `Claude turn failed`, delivery
  uncertain (conservative; unchanged; no Windows case observed).

## Decisions for root's catalogue (proposed, not blockers)

1. Unexplained refusal → `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED`, `retriable: false` (non-resumable for Claude, like
   existing EACCES/UNKNOWN). Previously ENOENT was `HARNESS_NOT_INSTALLED` (resumable) on a false
   claim. Alternative declined: `retriable: true` to keep resumability — would stretch
   "retriable" to a non-transient start failure.
2. Turn cwd missing/not a folder → `HARNESS_INVALID_CONFIGURATION` (pinned, non-resumable;
   engine shows `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED` + `adapterCode`). Alternative: generic `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED`
   (same resumability, less specific). Contract `WORKING_DIRECTORY_MISSING` exists but is unused;
   using it needs an engine mapping change (out of scope).
3. Included two fixes on the same start path beyond wording: unhandled ENOTCONN (natively proven)
   and the started-child error guard (controlled evidence only).

## Out-of-scope observations for root (not changed)

- Codex maps any `enoent` to `HARNESS_NOT_INSTALLED` (`packages/adapter-codex/src/events.ts:354`,
  `isolation.ts:177`) — same misdiagnosis class.
- `packages/infrastructure/src/process/scripts.ts` and `packages/adapter-codex/src/cli.ts` attach
  no stdout/stderr `error` handlers; the same uncaught ENOTCONN for a ≥260-char cwd is plausible
  but was not exercised.
- Host: symlink tests need Developer Mode or the symlink privilege; one transient SQLite `EBUSY`.

604:When the CLI fails a turn it reports the failure in the event stream (`error`, then `turn.failed`) and then exits with code 1; the SDK then throws `Codex Exec exited with code 1: <stderr>`, and the CLI's stderr is usually only its startup banner (`Reading prompt from stdin...`). That thrown error is read as the stderr evidence it carries, piece by piece: a stderr that is one structured provider error as a whole, or else each line, read from the structured provider error it holds (also after a prefix such as `ERROR: `) and as text otherwise, so a repeated provider error never reaches a message heuristic. A piece that exactly repeats evidence the stream reported (code, message, retry flag and submission metadata) adds nothing, whatever rank its text would get. Every other typed piece joins the evidence fold in order, so a later refusal, an authentication failure or a missing session beside a repeat is ranked like any other evidence. When nothing new and typed remains, the wrapper adds nothing if the stream reported the turn's failure, which includes fatal stream evidence (`turn.failed`, a terminal or pinned error) also after `turn.completed`; otherwise the wrapper is the cause (#243, PR #426 audit scans 2 and 3). content.content:
this manual trigger-start preflight; their existing execution checks remain in place and can
fail after earlier nodes have run. In particular, replay can return 202 with an unready harness,
execute preceding mutations, then fail when it reaches that harness. Unresolved child references
retain their existing `SUBLOOP_NOT_FOUND` execution behavior. Readiness is an admission-time
observation, not a guarantee of later account access.

`/harness/preflight` exposes seven server states. `checking` is a web-only request state.
`authenticated` is absent if login was not checked or could not be established; false requires
positive signed-out evidence. Claude parses auth-status JSON even on
exit 1 (`loggedIn:false` or an explicit nonempty non-Claude.ai account method). During auth status,
explicit `Not logged in` text on stdout or bounded stderr confirms sign-out even on exit 0.
Empty output, `{}` or an unrecognised login response on exit 0 is `unknown`, with no `authenticated` field;
a successful exit alone establishes no login fact. A recognised Claude.ai status or Codex
"Logged in" status establishes true; an explicit signed-out status establishes false.

No-turn diagnostic precedence is CLI-syntax errors first, explicit HTTP/API 401/403 (`auth`),
429 (`quota`) or 5xx (`transport`) next, then connection errors/wording, then quota/auth keywords.
Thus incidental "network" advice cannot override 401 or 429, while connection errors such as
`ECONNREFUSED` still outrank incidental auth words in server/refresh diagnostics. Version numbers
are not HTTP status evidence. For Claude's unstructured diagnostics, recognised stderr wins
over conflicting stdout because stderr is the CLI's primary error channel; stdout is consulted
when stderr is absent or classified `unknown`, so an unrelated warning cannot hide stdout quota.
Positive Claude auth-status sign-out evidence (structured or explicit text) is handled separately;
process start, timeout, cancellation, overflow and unconfirmed termination remain authoritative.
None of this inference applies to
model-turn stdout or changes turn retry eligibility.
Harness checks in `/system/preflight` carry state alongside the system's `ok`/`warn`/`fail`
severity. Each problem is one detail sentence and one action ending "then retry preflight"
(`readinessMessage` in the domain package); a specific detail, such as the CLI version below the
minimum or the missing option, replaces the generic one rather than being followed by it.
Web queries retain their existing two-second stale interval and focus refresh.

# Independent trace of F1 and F2 at the original source

Source: `a04f6661a74a727e6c963d8648ea2998bb6dbe7b`, `harness.ts` SHA-256
`bc45a1849e0b8ac7e4c89ecc423faa8511da5bee374200b90328469863e6bf1b` (git blob `91b00200`),
`process.ts` blob `740f92c3`. Written before any test or source change. Line numbers are the
original `harness.ts` unless stated.

## Producers (process.ts, unchanged by this work)

- `outputFault` (process.ts 220-224): a stdout or stderr `error` of a started child (pid set) sets
  `outputFailed = true` and calls `kill()`. If `killTree` confirms and `close` arrives, the result
  settles with the close code (1, null or any other), so `outputFailed` coexists with a nonzero or
  null `exitCode`.
- `finish` (process.ts 143-148): for a probe (`classifyDiagnostics`), `failureState` is
  `cliFailureState(stderr window)` whenever `exitCode !== 0` and stderr was seen, independent of
  `outputFailed`; `notLoggedIn` whenever stderr contains "not logged in".
- Spawn refusal (process.ts 229-240): no pid, `spawnCode` set, then one `stat` observation gives
  `startRefusal` (`working-directory-missing` / `-not-directory` / `executable-missing`) or none.

## F1 — auth check, output lost, exit 1 or null

`inspect().run(['auth','status','--json'], true)` (harness.ts 263-327):

1. 277-284: `JSON.parse(result.stdout)` of a truncated body throws; `auth` stays undefined, so no
   `signOutDetail` (285-299).
2. 300-310: the positive sign-out branch is taken only for `signOutDetail`, stdout "not logged in"
   or runner `notLoggedIn`. That branch calls `checkOutcome({...result, exitCode: 0})`, whose
   `exitCode: 0` skips the inference branch and reaches the `outputFailed` guard at 201 — already
   correct (existing test harness.test.ts:1175 exercises exactly this, at exit 0).
3. Otherwise 314-325 call `checkOutcome` with `failureState` = runner `failureState` (recognised
   stderr) or, when absent/`unknown`, `cliFailureState(stdout)` of the truncated body.
4. `checkOutcome` (157-215) order: termination-unconfirmed 163, abort 170, spawn refusal 171,
   timeout 172, overflow 178, callback 185, **inference 186-200** (`probe && exitCode !== 0 &&
   failureState not unknown`), **output guard 201-205**, exit/stdin 206-212.
5. With `exitCode` 1 or null and an inferred `auth`, 195 throws `HARNESS_NOT_AUTHENTICATED` with
   `readinessDetail('claude','auth')` = "Claude sign-in is missing or invalid." before 201 is
   reached. `quota` → `HARNESS_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED`; `transport` → `HARNESS_TRANSPORT_FAILED`,
   retriable; `cli-incompatible` → `HARNESS_CLI_INCOMPATIBLE`.
6. 360-361: `failureState(error) === 'auth'` sets `facts.authenticated = false`. 376-390 produce
   `state: 'auth'` (version/help passed, so it is the first failure) and the problem
   "Claude sign-in is missing or invalid. Run claude auth login, then retry preflight."
7. Turn: 442-443 throw `inspection.failures[0]` = that `HARNESS_NOT_AUTHENTICATED`; 571-578 emit it
   with `submission: 'definitely-not-submitted'`; no `--print` process starts.

Stdout example from the report: `{"authMethod":"claude.ai","email":"authentication@example.invalid`
→ `cliFailureState` matches `authenticat` (domain readiness.ts 30) → `auth`. Recognised stderr
example: `API Error: 401` → status 401 → `auth` in the runner.

Not affected: exit 0 with output loss (inference branch requires `exitCode !== 0`); positive
sign-out text/JSON with output loss (step 2); turns (`probe` false; turn output loss is caught in
the precedence block at 519-527 and reported as "Claude turn failed").

Smallest correction: test `probe && result.outputFailed` before the inference branch, after the
callback check. Termination, abort, refusal, deadline, overflow and callback stay ahead of it.

## F2 — version passes, only the help check fails with a process cause

`inspect()` 328-352:

1. 329-331: version succeeds; `version` = e.g. `2.1.285`.
2. 335: help `run(...)`. Causes it can throw, all `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED` unless noted:
   a. spawn refusal → `startFailure(code, refusal, cwd, true)` (112-152): check folder missing /
      not a folder (127-131, new in #364); unexplained refusal "Claude CLI could not be started
      (ENOENT)." or the long-TEMP wording (139-145, new in #364 for ENOENT; pre-#364 probe ENOENT
      was `HARNESS_NOT_INSTALLED`, which the wrapper never touched; pre-#364 EACCES/UNKNOWN had the
      same short text and was already wrapped); executable missing → `HARNESS_NOT_INSTALLED`
      (passes through).
   b. output loss at exit 0 → 201 "Claude CLI check output could not be read." (new in #364);
      at exit 1/null with recognised stderr the F1 order first yields an inferred state
      (`cli-incompatible` → `HARNESS_CLI_INCOMPATIBLE`).
   c. ordinary option failure: exit ≠ 0 / stdin failure → "Claude CLI check exited with code N." /
      "stopped without an exit code." (206-212); recognised "unknown option" stderr →
      `HARNESS_CLI_INCOMPATIBLE` (186-200).
   d. termination unconfirmed / timeout / overflow → their own codes; abort → `DOMException`.
3. 336-347: the wrapper replaces every `HARNESS_CLI_INCOMPATIBLE` or `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED` with
   "Claude CLI <version> failed the --max-turns/--help check." — so 2a (folder, unexplained,
   long-TEMP) and 2b lose their fixed cause; 2c is the intended target; 2d and NOT_INSTALLED pass.
4. 350-352 push it; auth (354-363) runs independently and may succeed (`authenticated: true`).
5. 376-390: `state` `unknown`, problem "Claude CLI 2.1.285 failed the --max-turns/--help check.
   Check that the Claude CLI starts and responds, then retry preflight."; the fixed cause is absent
   from the whole response.
6. Turn: 442-443 throw that same wrapped error; no `--print` process starts.

Existing tests miss both: harness.test.ts:1155 refuses every command (version fails first);
1175 faults auth only, at exit 0 with explicit sign-out handling; 718 is the ordinary exit-1 help
failure (the intended wrapper target).

Smallest correction consistent with D193: a module-private subclass of `ClaudeHarnessError`, fixed
to `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED`/not retriable, constructed only where `startFailure` reports a probe start
refusal and where `checkOutcome` reports lost probe output; the help wrapper skips instances of it.
No message matching, no exported type, no code/retriability/message change, no process.ts change.

# 06 - Harness integration

Each inference node selects its harness through `config.harness`, defaulting to `codex`.
Loop settings supply per-harness model and effort defaults; loop-level harness input is rejected.
Decision routes and temporary boolean predicates use the Codex decider; structured repair uses the structured-completion port. See
[ADR-0019](decisions/ADR-0019-inference-node-harness.md) and
[ADR-0023](decisions/ADR-0023-installed-claude-code.md).

## Native Chat workflow integration (#443)

Native Chat is an entry point into the existing engine, not a second inference implementation.
The gateway seeds one system loop with **Trigger → Inference → Context mutation → Exit**. It uses normal harness
selection, model/effort defaults and readiness checks. The inference captures plain text; the
ordinary Context mutation constructs the exact response envelope deterministically.
Seeding and device pairing make no provider request and do not silently choose a discovered model.
Each turn pins the published definition and effective defaults through native admission.
Missing CLI/authentication/model prerequisites produce actionable readiness before a new turn is
admitted; there is no substitute reply or provider failover.
The minimal system seed can exist published before model setup; it cannot send until ready.

The seeded inference node starts a fresh session in a temporary working directory. Its prompt
receives the current text and server-built bounded conversation history. The existing harness
policy applies: [ADR-0063](decisions/ADR-0063-loop-turns-without-personal-extensions.md) is amended
by [ADR-0067](decisions/ADR-0067-codex-inherits-configured-plugins.md), so Codex inherits configured
plugins and their tools/services while standalone MCP discovery and other isolation defaults remain.
Owners may edit the workflow's interior, including its harness, prompt, model, effort,
scripts, decisions and awaited subloops. Native Chat does not sandbox arbitrary owner-authored
Script commands or introduce a smart-home routing provider. Guided transcription is an ordinary
Script normalizer described below.

The loop boundary uses the canonical `graphgoblin.chat.v1` input schema from
`packages/contracts/src/chat.ts`. The server supplies `conversationId`, `requestId`, turn counter,
current input and recent valid history. A text input is `{kind: 'text', text}`. An audio input is
`{kind: 'audio', audio: {id, mimeType, bytes, path}, caption?}`; only the server can resolve the private
absolute path. A client sends an upload id, never a path or URL. The server limits history to the
most recent twelve valid completed turn pairs and 64,000 characters, dropping oldest whole pairs.

The boundary requires one manual trigger named `chat-input`, exposed to exactly UI and API, and
the canonical `chatResponse` variable schema. The deterministic Context mutation writes the
response into `/vars/chatResponse`. Every successful exit returns exactly `vars.chatResponse` to
exactly the caller. Failure/exhausted exits may return none or that same canonical response; they
never become successful assistant messages. The public response is exactly
`{protocol: 'graphgoblin.chat.v1', reply: '<nonblank text>'}`. Strings, `text`, `message` and arbitrary
JSON are not reply aliases. The chat projection validates a successful native result again on
read, so an invalid result is `CHAT_RESPONSE_INVALID` without a reply or future-history entry.

Draft saves refuse changes to the locked trigger identity/type/exposure/canonical schema and the
`chatResponse` variable schema. Other boundary wiring issues remain saveable and block
publication/admission. A generic system-loop start, draft test or Subloop accepts text-only
protocol input, even when its published loop supports audio. Only native chat admission resolves
a new audio reference. Verified immutable native replay may retain the source audio; a new start
or caller-supplied replay id cannot grant path authority.

### Configure an audio normalizer

Audio is unavailable in the default text-only loop. To enable it, replace the trigger input schema
with the exported canonical audio-capable schema and make `chat-normalize` the only node directly
after `chat-input`. Use one of these native node configurations:

| Node    | Required configuration                                                                       | Recorded text                                                                                 |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Script  | `stdin: 'thread'`, `stdout: 'last-output'`; return JSON `{text}`                             | `thread.outputs['chat-normalize'].value.text`                                                 |
| Subloop | `output.mode: 'result-only'`, `output.resultTo.lastOutput: true`; the child returns `{text}` | `thread.outputs['chat-normalize'].value.result.text`, with its envelope `status: 'succeeded'` |

Successful Script output continues to the protected check. Unhandled exit codes fail normally;
an existing explicit exit-code mapping to `out` retains its native meaning.

The normalizer must handle text pass-through as well as audio transcription. The protected chain
is `chat-input.out → chat-normalize.out → chat-normalize-check`: the canonical expression decision
continues through `valid` into the authored workflow or through `invalid` into the failure exit
`chat-normalize-invalid` (`outcome: 'failure'`, `returns: 'none'`, no destinations). Input, normalizer
and check cannot be revisited or bypassed; the failure exit accepts only that invalid edge.
The check validates the original recorded Script object or succeeded Subloop result before a
later model/action runs. It requires exactly one key, `text`, whose nonblank string is at most
16,000 UTF-16 code units. Unknown fields, blank/overlength text and a malformed Subloop envelope
fail without continuing to later actions. Expression errors fail safely too; no coercion/repair
changes transcript content.

Use the domain's `enableChatAudio(definition, normalizer)` and `disableChatAudio(definition)`
helpers to change the canonical trigger/normalizer/check/failure chain as one edit. Enabling refuses
ambiguous continuation wiring and reserved-id collisions. Disabling can also remove a partial
chain: it uses exactly one valid existing check continuation, or requires an explicit
`{continuationNodeId}` naming an ordinary nontrigger step (`SYSTEM_CHAT_CONTINUATION_REQUIRED`).
It removes reserved voice nodes/incident edges and existing trigger-outgoing edges, restores one
trigger continuation and leaves other ordinary nodes/edges intact. For the exact untouched seed prompt,
they also switch its input reference; they do not rewrite arbitrary owner prompts. Custom
interiors must consume the recorded normalized text described above. Subloops already await their
child; do not add a `wait` property or change the native subloop result envelope. The projector
selects the extractor from the pinned node kind and independently validates the recorded value.
The owner editor exposes these edits as **Set up voice messages**, **Add voice steps** and
**Turn off voice messages**. Setup stages a real Script/Subloop configuration without executing
it; publication remains a separate action.

The normalized text must contain 1–16,000 nonblank UTF-16 code units. For an audio turn, a successful raw
run without a valid recorded normalizer result becomes `CHAT_AUDIO_NORMALIZATION_INVALID` and
does not display a reply or enter future history. A model-generated guess is never a transcript.
The session's **Configured by loop** state establishes this static contract only: an unavailable
executable or malformed external result still fails at runtime. The guided preset adds tested
Whisper.cpp and OpenAI routes; arbitrary custom normalizers remain the owner’s responsibility.
There is no browser speech-recognition fallback or speech synthesis.

Audio files live in the private `<dataDir>/chat-audio/` directory and retain their bytes for the
owner's normalizer. Unused uploads expire after one hour. Consumed files remain available while
the linked native run/history can reference them and are cleaned up with history ownership,
preserving restart recovery. They are not artifacts encoded into event text or publicly served
files. Retained used/unused/in-flight audio is capped at 64 MiB per audience and 256 MiB per gateway;
exceeding the quota refuses an upload without deleting referenced inputs. Deletion of one turn
does not retroactively erase its text from later immutable native histories. See
[the Chat frontend](09-frontend-and-pwa.md#native-chat-and-the-goblin-pwa-443) and
[ADR-0065](decisions/ADR-0065-native-chat-system-loops-and-device-pairing.md).

### Plain text capture and context admission (ADR-0068)

`output.capture: 'text'` preserves `finalText` exactly as a string, including JSON-looking answers.
It cannot be combined with an output schema. Leaving this optional field unset is equivalent to
`auto`, retaining strict existing
JSON/schema validation for other workflows; malformed structured output is never salvaged by
selecting a convenient object. The standard chat seed uses text capture and an editable 300-second
inference deadline. Existing published loops are not rewritten when the seed changes; reads keep
omitted capture fields and their existing draft tokens unchanged.

Ollama admission budgets the complete rendered prompt, model wrapper and output reserve before
sending it. Only recognized standard chat prompts may omit oldest complete history pairs. The
stored input/history stays intact and the turn exposes retained/omitted counts. Custom prompts
are never truncated. Required input that cannot fit is refused before dispatch with
`INFERENCE_CONTEXT_LIMIT`; unknown context profiles produce `INFERENCE_CONTEXT_UNSUPPORTED`.

The initial qualified profile is deliberately narrow: Ollama 0.32.15, Qwen3.5 with the observed
GPT-2/Qwen35 byte tokenizer, the unmodified single-user renderer, no preset system/messages and
`none` effort. Its allocation is at most 4096 tokens, with a 1024-token reply reserve, a 512-token
wrapper allowance and a conservative UTF-8 byte ceiling for prompt/schema input. This is not an
exact tokenizer count or the model’s advertised maximum. Other discovered models remain visible
with an unsupported/unverified reason until their profile is qualified; discovery, readiness and
dispatch share the same policy. Enabled choices/defaults are preserved. Requalification is required
when the runtime/profile changes; discovery alone is not memory or performance evidence.

### Guided voice preset (ADR-0068)

Settings → Voice saves gateway-owned configuration with revision checks. A pure preview adds the
ordinary `graphgoblin-voice-normalize` Script with a non-secret configuration snapshot; explicit
staging checks the reviewed configuration revision and loop draft hash atomically. Publishing is
separate. Device clones are listed individually. A custom normalizer is opened for manual review,
never overwritten. An editor handoff refuses dirty/restored/conflicting drafts, pauses autosave
while staging and preserves Undo after the saved baseline changes.

Local transcription uses a separately qualified Whisper.cpp executable and a verified small
English model. The guided downloader installs only immutable allowlisted model bytes, with exact
size/SHA-256, disk bounds and atomic publication; it does not install a compiler, runtime or ffmpeg.
Runtime/dependency qualification is server-owned private evidence, not a browser claim or a
version-string check. Unsupported machines can use the guided cloud connection. The setup test
transcribes a short public speech sample, records latency and unused-memory telemetry and expires its
result; changing runtime/model/configuration requires another test. Test while the usual Ollama
model is running before relying on local coexistence.

The cloud adapter uses a dedicated `voice.openai.*` secret and OpenAI transcription. Setup names
provider billing and requires acknowledgement before uploading the public sample. The chosen route
is disclosed before Send and pinned before transcription. Auto prefers a suitable local route;
cloud is used only when explicitly configured/permitted. A failed or uncertain dispatch never
silently fails over to another provider or retries a command. Text needs neither route. Caption
text precedes the transcript, and the protected canonical `{text}` check validates the combined
input before inference or other workflow actions.

## The harness port (Decided)

```ts
interface HarnessPort {
  id: 'codex' | 'claude' | 'ollama'; // LiteLLM is a recorded later adapter idea
  preflight(): Promise<{
    state: HarnessReadinessState;
    ok: boolean;
    version?: string;
    authenticated?: boolean;
    problems: string[];
    authMethod?: 'claude.ai' | null;
    supportedPolicies?: ClaudePolicy[];
    models?: ClaudeModelCapability[];
  }>;
  start(req: HarnessStartRequest, signal: AbortSignal): HarnessSession;
  resume(sessionId: string, req: HarnessStartRequest, signal: AbortSignal): HarnessSession;
}

type HarnessStartRequest = {
  workingDirectory: string;
  model?: string;
  effort?: Effort;
  options: InferenceConfig['harnessOptions'];
  capabilities?: InferenceConfig['capabilities'];
  turn: HarnessTurnRequest;
};
type HarnessTurnRequest = { prompt: string; outputSchema?: JsonSchema };

interface HarnessSession {
  sessionId: Promise<string>; // resolves as soon as the harness reports it
  events: AsyncIterable<HarnessEvent>; // normalised, see below
  result: Promise<HarnessResult>;
  cancel(): Promise<void>;
}

type HarnessEvent =
  | { type: 'session'; sessionId: string; mode: 'fresh' | 'resumed' }
  | { type: 'item'; item: HarnessItem } // message, reasoning summary, command, file change, tool call, search
  | { type: 'usage'; inputTokens: number; outputTokens: number; cached?: number }
  | {
      type: 'submitted';
      marker:
        | 'claude.assistant'
        | 'claude.result'
        | 'codex.turn.started'
        | 'ollama.response'
        | 'fake.accepted';
    }
  | { type: 'turn-complete' }
  | {
      type: 'error';
      code: string;
      message: string;
      retriable: boolean;
      submission: PromptSubmission;
    };

type HarnessResult = {
  finalText: string;
  structured?: unknown;
  usage: Usage;
  items: HarnessItem[];
};
```

Adapters translate native events into this model. The engine never sees SDK types.

## Native Ollama and discovered models (#443)

Ollama is a native Inference harness implemented in `packages/infrastructure/src/ollama/` through
the Node HTTP transport. It calls `/api/chat` directly with the exact selected model identifier,
the already-rendered prompt as one user message, streaming enabled and the node's JSON Schema
when present. It uses no CLI, OpenAI compatibility shim, external SDK or standalone chat worker.
The existing engine still owns prompt/context transforms, structured-output validation,
transcripts, usage, cancellation and recovery. Ollama is an Inference option; generic LLM
decision evaluation and structured repair retain their existing provider contracts.

### Connect and discover

One gateway-wide connection supplies the gateway-wide model catalog. Configure its origin and
enabled state in Settings. Before a saved connection exists, the defaults are
`GG_OLLAMA_ENABLED=true` and `GG_OLLAMA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434`; a saved connection takes
precedence. An origin may use HTTP or HTTPS and must contain no credentials, query, fragment or
path beyond `/`. The owner may select a local/LAN service or a trusted proxy; not every selected
server or model is necessarily local. GraphGoblin does not install/start Ollama, forward its
management key, manage proxy credentials or download/pull models.
Services requiring sign-in are unsupported by this adapter; it sends no authentication credential.

Startup schedules discovery immediately after storage is ready. Saving, enabling or changing a
connection also attempts it immediately, then an enabled gateway refreshes every five minutes
without Settings being open. **Refresh Ollama models** beside the model list requests a refresh
and coalesces with one already running. A connection save remains saved when discovery fails;
the returned discovery state explains the failure. Disabling or stopping cancels scheduled
discovery. Saving the connection off also blocks all new Ollama HTTP work and closes open gateway
discovery/preflight/inference requests; work already accepted by the remote server may continue.
No unload/remote-stop request is sent. A response/status from a prior connection revision cannot
overwrite the current catalog or discovery status.

Discovery reads `/api/tags` and bounded `/api/show` metadata. A complete snapshot reconciles the
catalog atomically. A partial/failed scan preserves the previous complete snapshot and last
success time; a successful empty list marks previously known models missing. Scans are bounded to
256 models, four concurrent detail reads, five seconds per metadata request, thirty seconds per
scan and 2 MiB per response. Cached details are invalidated when their digest or connection changes.
These operations never generate text, load/unload a model or change owner defaults.

Discovered rows use the exact server-reported names, namespaces and tags and remain harness-managed:
the owner can enable/disable them, not edit their metadata or delete them. A newly supported model
starts enabled; refreshes preserve the owner's enabled preference, stored selections and defaults.
Missing or unsupported rows remain visible with their availability reason. They cannot start new
runs, but reappearance can restore availability without losing that preference. Availability and
enablement are separate: `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` is not `MODEL_DISABLED`. Catalog, picker, publication
and runtime resolution read the same availability facts. A server outage does not erase the last
complete catalog; service readiness can still block a run. A model removed between discovery and
dispatch fails visibly without substitution or an automatic pull. The recorded digest is discovery
metadata, not a guarantee that an Ollama tag always points to immutable weights.

After startup migrations, current connection state governs public/runtime catalog reads. Off projects **Ollama is off
in Settings**, and metadata from a different/absent connection revision projects **Not yet listed
at the new address**. Both use unavailable `missing` state while preserving the snapshot and
owner Enabled choice. An address change does not pretend old models were checked at the new
origin; only a complete current enabled-revision scan restores availability. Failed scans retain
usable last-complete availability only within the same revision, never across origins.

An explicit structurally valid Ollama process model in `GG_DEFAULTS.byHarness.ollama` defers
